coverage_notes:
SOURCES USED. The single best source is the official "Nebraska Football, 1994 Media Guide," scanned on the Internet Archive. All quotes below are taken from its OCR plain-text derivative at https://archive.org/download/nebraska-football-1994-media-guide-c/Nebraska%20Football%2C%201994%20Media%20Guide%20%28C%29_djvu.txt and were mechanically verified as exact substrings of that file before submission. IMPORTANT FOR THE MATCHER: quotes must be checked against that _djvu.txt URL, not the archive.org /details/ landing page. The text is OCR of a printed guide, so it contains genuine OCR artifacts that I preserved verbatim rather than correcting — e.g. "Grantis in his first yearas a gradu-", "Mary Lyn Winingeris inher 12th year", "andGlenda Quarles", hyphenated line-break splits, and curly apostrophes in some lines but straight ones in others. Do not normalize these. I deliberately used single-line quotes because the OCR wraps mid-sentence; several quotes therefore end mid-sentence or mid-word. Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_Nebraska_Cornhuskers_football_team) is used as a corroborating second source for the head coach, the nine on-field assistants, and Boyd Epley; its infobox separates each name from its role with HTML markup, so the Wikipedia quotes are the role phrases alone ("14th season as DC/DL coach", etc.), which are contiguous and unique in the rendered page.

WHAT IS COMPLETE. The on-field tier is complete and unambiguous: head coach plus exactly nine full-time assistants, matching the NCAA limit of the era, and Wikipedia and the media guide agree on all ten names. The graduate-assistant tier is also believed complete: NCAA rules in 1994 capped teams at two football graduate assistants, and the guide profiles exactly two (Clayton Carlin, Mike Grant). The strength and conditioning tier is complete as the guide presents it; note the guide describes Epley heading "a staff of five full-time strength coaches," and I list five full-timers (Epley, Arthur, Bailey, Gobel, Thompson) plus one strength GA (Coleman) and Paul Koch.

WHAT I COULD NOT RECOVER, STATED PLAINLY.
1. Analyst and quality-control tiers: I found ZERO. These job titles did not meaningfully exist in 1994 college football; the roles were not on the staff, rather than being undocumented. No rows are included and none should be expected.
2. Archived school athletics staff directory: NOT RECOVERABLE. Source #2 in the task brief cannot be satisfied for this season. huskers.com did not exist in 1994, and the Wayback Machine's earliest crawls begin in late 1996, so there is no archived fall-1994 or January-1995 Nebraska staff directory to consult. The media guide substitutes for it.
3. Mid-season changes: I searched for 1994 in-season Nebraska staff arrivals/departures and found none documented. No midseason_note is set on any row. Caveat: the media guide is a PRESEASON publication (printed August 1994), so it cannot by itself confirm that every listed person was still on staff at the January 1, 1995 Orange Bowl. I found no contemporary report of any change, but treat this as "no evidence of change" rather than positively verified continuity. Kevin Steele's departure to the Carolina Panthers occurred AFTER the championship game, so he was on staff at the title game.
4. Student-tier personnel: the guide names 17 student athletic trainers (Reid Brakke, Zane Harvey, Josh Heller, Yuko Ishida, Jason Jenkins, Jennifer Linden, David Maloley, Robin Marshall, Jason Masek, Dannika Nelson, Jen Ogle, Matt Olberding, Peggy Pope, Jason Riley, Matt Svoboda, Stacia Weaver, Jennifer Wunder). I deliberately EXCLUDED these as students rather than staff; they are recoverable from the same page if the dataset wants them. Student equipment managers and football student managers are NOT documented anywhere I could find.
5. Recruiting staff below Pederson: only the recruiting secretary (Kathi Woody) is documented. Nebraska had no separate recruiting-coordinator title on the 1994 football staff.

SCOPE CAVEAT ON DEPARTMENT-WIDE ROWS, PLEASE READ BEFORE COUNTING RINGS. Nebraska in 1994 ran medical, video, academic, and part of strength as ATHLETIC-DEPARTMENT-WIDE units serving all 22 sports, not as football-only staffs. I included them because they are named in the football media guide and the brief asked for support staff where documented, but they are not equivalent to football-only employees. Specifically: George Sullivan is the only medical person explicitly football-designated ("Head FB Trainer," and his bio says he will focus entirely on football that fall). Jerry Weber, Doak Ostergard, Jack Nickolite, Dr. Lonnie Albers, Duke LaRue, Cindy Barker, Sara Weinberg, and the five athletic-training graduate assistants (Cook, Edwards, Froiland, Gardner, Quarles) serve the whole department. Paul Koch's own bio says he works with basketball and Olympic sports, NOT football — he is included only because the guide prints him among the football-section strength staff, and he is the most likely row to want to drop. Dennis Leblanc and Keith Zimmer are academic-support staff for all sports, though Zimmer's bio explicitly mentions assisting with football. Of the video staff I included only Dave Finn (whose directory phone number, 472-3116, is the football office line) and John Bousek (whose bio explicitly counts his tenure in FOOTBALL seasons); I excluded department video staff Floyd Sorley, Vince Ullman, Bryan Carpenter, and Jeff Schmahl, who are documented in the same guide but described in department-wide terms — they can be added from the same source if desired.

NOTHING IS PADDED. Every row has a verbatim quote verified present in the cited source. No name was inferred, recalled from memory, or included on plausibility.
